title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 160 (Right of persons other than retiring directors to stand for directorship)

content.overview: Section 160 allows a person who is not a retiring director to stand for directorship if written notice of candidature is left at the registered office at least fourteen days before the meeting, with the prescribed deposit. The company must inform members of the candidature. The deposit is refunded if the candidate is elected or obtains more than twenty-five per cent of the total valid votes cast.
content.glance: Non-retiring candidate: 14 days’ notice + prescribed deposit; company informs members; deposit refunded on election or >25% votes.
content.study: A person who is not a retiring director shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, be eligible for appointment to the office of a director at any general meeting, if he, or some member intending to propose him, has, not less than fourteen days before the meeting, left at the registered office of the company a notice in writing under his hand signifying his candidature as a director or, as the case may be, the intention of such member to propose him as a candidate for that office, along with the deposit of such sum as may be prescribed. The company must inform its members of the candidature in the prescribed manner. The deposit is refunded to the person if he is elected as a director or gets more than twenty-five per cent of total valid votes cast either on show of hands or on poll on such resolution. Current-law framing: identify non-retiring candidate; check 14-day notice and deposit; confirm company notice to members; apply refund rule.

sections.heading: Who May Stand
sections.body: A person who is not a retiring director, subject to the Act.

sections.heading: Notice and Deposit
sections.body: Written notice at the registered office at least fourteen days before the meeting, with the prescribed deposit, by the candidate or a proposing member.

sections.heading: Company’s Duty
sections.body: Inform members of the candidature in the prescribed manner.

sections.heading: Deposit Refund
sections.body: Refunded if the candidate is elected or obtains more than twenty-five per cent of total valid votes cast.

provisions.title: Right of persons other than retiring directors to stand for directorship

examples.title: Valid candidature
examples.body: A non-retiring person leaves written notice and the prescribed deposit at the registered office 20 days before the AGM. Section 160 is satisfied; the company must inform members.

examples.title: Deposit refund
examples.body: The candidate is not elected but obtains 30% of valid votes. The deposit is refundable under s. 160.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 160 apply to a retiring director seeking reappointment?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 160 addresses persons other than retiring directors. Retiring directors seeking reappointment follow the rotation and reappointment route under s. 152.

distinctions.title: Right to stand for directorship (s. 160) vs appointment of directors (s. 152)

rows.left: How a non-retiring person gets on the ballot
rows.right: How directors are appointed and rotate

misconceptions.trap: Any person can demand appointment without notice or deposit.
misconceptions.correction: Section 160 requires at least fourteen days’ written notice at the registered office and the prescribed deposit.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 160 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm non-retiring candidate. II. Check 14-day notice and deposit. III. Company notice to members. IV. Refund rule. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Candidature facts; notice and deposit; company communication; vote outcome; precise relief.
